attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: 'Aren't going away' firmly predicts that the problem will last. It has no deadline. Reading 'like hallucinations' as an example of scope, and 'going way' as a typo for 'going away', is fair.

contract.note: The plain reading (hallucinations stay a material problem) is ordinary. The contract rightly says that persistence over a finite period cannot settle an open-ended forecast, and that only a replicated demonstration that hallucinations have been eliminated can contradict it.

evidence.note: A Sept 2025 preprint, published before the evaluation date, reports that hallucinations persist in state-of-the-art systems. This supports the forecast so far but cannot settle an open-ended claim.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The evidence shows hallucinations persisting through 2025, which is consistent with the claim. No replicated demonstration that they were eliminated appears in the packet, so the forecast is not contradicted. Persistence up to a finite date cannot conclusively support an open-ended forecast, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Truly astonished' expresses high confidence that the milestone will not be reached by end-2024, so it is scored as a forecast. The drafter's 'very unlikely' slightly softens this into probability wording, but it keeps the threshold (human expert levels) and the deadline.

contract.note: Reading the claim as broad factual reliability comparable to matched experts is the ordinary reading and is not stretched. The result depends on that reading versus parity on one narrow task, which the speaker did not specify.

evidence.note: The SimpleQA paper (Nov 2024) has a trainer verification exercise. It is not a matched comparison between models and experts, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The deadline of 2024-12-31 has passed. The packet has no verified matched evaluation showing broad expert-level parity, or its absence, for systems available by then. The possible counterevidence from the physician-summary study could not be read. SimpleQA is context only, so the evidence does not settle the outcome.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps all three parts of the present-state observation. Treating 'keeping people up at night' as concern, not literal sleep loss, is fair.

contract.note: The 2023 to March 2024 window and the reading 'little money relative to costs' were chosen by the evaluator but are ordinary. The money part turns on revenue versus profit, which the speaker did not specify.

evidence.note: Cisco survey with fieldwork in 2023: 27% of organisations had banned GenAI, at least temporarily, over privacy and security. This supports widespread concern among professionals. It is Cisco's survey of other organisations, not a disclosure about Cisco itself.
The March 2024 Morris II worm paper demonstrates attacks on GenAI email assistants. This supports material security weaknesses under the tested conditions.

reviews.rationale: The security and concern parts are supported by e2 and e1. No matched financial evidence was verified for the 'isn't making much money' part. Because one of three asserted parts is neither supported nor contradicted, the composite claim cannot be scored as a whole.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical remark in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the causal chain: similar models, so no moat, so heavy price competition. It concerns the market at the time of the post.

contract.note: Reading 'moat' as a durable advantage and requiring the whole chain to hold is a fair reading. Whether 'moat' covers only the model or the whole business is unspecified and could decide the result.

evidence.note: a16z research from March 2024 says enterprises see model performance converging and design their applications for easy switching. This supports the similarity part and partly the no-moat part. The source is an investor survey, not representative.
Cloud ties and procurement influenced which model enterprises chose, which hints at advantages beyond the model itself. Their durability is not shown.
OpenAI's own disclosure records large API price cuts in Nov 2023. It does not attribute them to competition rather than cost savings.

reviews.rationale: The evidence supports model convergence and price cuts. It does not show that durable advantages were absent; cloud ties may count as advantages. It also does not separate competition from efficiency gains as the cause of the price cuts. The causal chain is neither established nor refuted.
